name: 42497-longprefill-230b-4gpu
hardware: 4x H100 80GB HBM3 -- half of one a3 node (--gres=gpu:4).
parallelism: TP=4, PP=1, DP=1, no expert parallelism, one in-process vLLM engine; no router in front, no external cache tier, no KV connector. 230 GB of weights does not fit below TP=4.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=16, warmup 25%, cooldown 10%, bounded at 160 requests with a 900 s safety cap, static seed 42497.
workload: synthetic `synthetic_text`, 8192 prompt tokens in and exactly 1024 tokens out per request, min == max on both, single turn.
purpose: A long-document analysis assistant for 16 concurrent users, generating page-length answers from book-length prompts on four GPUs.
launch:
# The engine's command line. The engine is the commit named by the setup card
# (v0.21.1rc0-42-g966903eb93a0): do not add keys from a later vLLM, an argument this
# engine does not know is an error at construction.

model: MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7
tensor-parallel-size: 4
trust-remote-code: true
# An override: prefix caching is ON by default on this engine.
enable-prefix-caching: false
# The workload's worst case is 8192 + 1024 = 9216 tokens; the checkpoint's window is 204800.
max-model-len: 16384

# The batching point, stated rather than inherited.
#
# The oracle row this item reproduces was taken with a plain `vllm serve` on an 80 GB Hopper
# card, which is UsageContext.OPENAI_API_SERVER. `EngineArgs.get_batch_defaults` (arg_utils.py
# 2258-2266) branches on `device_memory >= 70 GiB and "a100" not in device_name` and hands that
# context 8192 / 1024. The two numbers below are therefore the source's own operating point,
# not a tuning choice.
#
# They have to be written down because this harness does NOT reach that branch. guidellm's
# vllm_python backend builds the engine with `AsyncLLMEngine.from_engine_args(engine_args)` and
# no usage context, so `usage_context` keeps its signature default of UsageContext.ENGINE_CONTEXT
# (v1/engine/async_llm.py:236). ENGINE_CONTEXT is not a key in either defaults dict -- they hold
# only LLM_CLASS and OPENAI_API_SERVER -- so `.get(usage_context, ...)` at arg_utils.py:2411 and
# 2416 misses and falls through to SchedulerConfig.DEFAULT_MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS = 2048 and
# DEFAULT_MAX_NUM_SEQS = 128 (config/scheduler.py:42-44), whose own docstring says they are
# "mainly for convenience when testing".
#
# It is load-bearing for THIS mechanism, not just for fidelity. At 2048 an 8192-token prompt is
# prefilled in 4 chunks of 2048 instead of 1 chunk of 8192, and the fused SiLU+Mul+FP8-quant
# kernel sees 2048 x top-8 = 16,384 MoE rows per forward instead of 65,536 -- a different point
# on the row-count curve the change is characterised against.
#
# 8192 >= the 8192-token prompt, so each prefill is one forward, as it was for the source.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
max-num-seqs: 1024
